scope: Current-main native Rust versus candidate only; no Python performance claim. Identical harness, one worker, independent release target directories; CPU 0 for original batches and CPU 1 for the documented focused recheck. All processes verified input SHA and exact ordered result/score/detail/selection SHA. VmHWM is process-lifetime peak, not incremental matcher memory. Rejected experiments and preliminary dense-only observations are retained. Final measurements use five paired fresh-process rounds, one recorded first-call warmup and 51 timed calls per small/medium control, five calls per large process, then 101 calls per focused recheck process. Full per-call arrays and raw result reports remain in ignored target/jaccard-long-overhead; this committed compact summary preserves process medians/ranges/counts and paired ratios. Binary revision association is declared from isolated builds, not inferred from executables. Dirty provisional snapshots are identified by recorded source SHA overrides. All three long-disjoint CPU batches are retained; benefit/regression is inconclusive. The old experiment command arrays are omitted here as redundant with settings/input fingerprints; their full arrays remain in the cited ignored reports. No numeric statistics were removed.
